conclusion.justification: The report concludes that high-quality randomized evidence clearly shows systemic corticosteroids like dexamethasone reduce the risk of death and improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients. Therefore, it endorses the claim that these drugs increase survival among critically ill patients.

report:
**Conclusion:** No—dexamethasone and related systemic corticosteroids do not *ensure* survival, but high-quality randomized evidence shows they **reduce the chance of death** in hospitalized COVID-19 patients who are critically ill or need supplemental oxygen.

In the RECOVERY randomized trial, dexamethasone lowered 28-day mortality in patients on invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs 41.4% with usual care) and produced a smaller benefit in those receiving oxygen without ventilation. It did **not** help patients who did not need respiratory support. [https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436)

A prospective meta-analysis of seven randomized trials in critically ill patients likewise found systemic corticosteroids (principally dexamethasone or hydrocortisone) associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality versus usual care/placebo. [https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279)

WHO recommends systemic corticosteroids for severe or critical COVID-19, because they dampen harmful inflammation; they should be used under clinical supervision, as they can have adverse effects and are not appropriate simply for mild COVID-19. [https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-dexamethasone](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-dexamethasone)
